tags: why do dogs sit on your feet
script: You sit down and, within seconds, your dog drops right on top of your feet. It's one of the most common dog habits, and it usually means several things at once. First, it's affection, since dogs seek physical contact with the people they trust, and your feet are a convenient place to rest. Second, it's a way of staying close, because if you stand up, they'll feel it right away and can follow you. Some dogs also do it to keep an eye on you and make sure you don't wander off without them. It can also be a mild form of attention seeking, especially if your dog got a pet or a kind word in the past after doing it. Confident dogs sometimes claim a favorite spot this way, but that's usually just comfort, not an attempt to control you. Anxious dogs may also use it as reassurance. If it's causing trouble, such as when you're cooking, teach a simple go-to-your-mat cue and reward them generously. Otherwise, it's one of the sweetest signs that your dog simply wants to be near you.
